# httpkit

```go
import "gorontalo/pkg/httpkit"
```

Package httpkit collects net/http presets for building services: ready\-made handlers and the shared conventions they rely on. It has no third\-party dependencies.

### Sub\\\-packages

Each handler is its own package; import the one you need directly. This package does not re\-export them, so the import path is the discovery path:

- gorontalo/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck — health, liveness, and readiness endpoints for orchestrators such as Kubernetes.
- gorontalo/pkg/httpkit/stdwrapper — adapts application handlers to a standard request/response contract \(request ID, response envelope, error\-code header, logging, panic recovery\).

New presets are added as sibling sub\-packages under gorontalo/pkg/httpkit and listed here, so this comment stays the index of what the kit offers.

### Shared contracts

This package itself holds only what is shared across those sub\-packages or useful without any of them, not forwarded copies of their symbols.

It re\-exports the standard header names the handlers use so callers can reference them without importing a specific handler sub\-package. They are grouped under the Headers namespace:

```
req.Header.Get(httpkit.Headers.RequestID)
resp.Header.Get(httpkit.Headers.ErrorCode)
```

It also provides DecodeJSON, a generic helper that decodes a request body into a struct and reports failures as a 400 standard error:

```
body, err := httpkit.DecodeJSON[CreateUser](r)
```

## Variables

<a name="Headers"></a>Headers holds the standard HTTP header names used by httpkit's handlers. Reference a field rather than hardcoding the string, e.g. httpkit.Headers.RequestID.

```go
var Headers = headerNames{
    RequestID: stdwrapper.HeaderRequestID,
    ErrorCode: stdwrapper.HeaderErrorCode,
}
```

<a name="DecodeJSON"></a>
## func [DecodeJSON](<https://github.com/xwinata/gorontalo/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/decodejson.go#L43>)

```go
func DecodeJSON[T any](r *http.Request) (T, error)
```

DecodeJSON reads r's body and decodes it into a value of type T. It is the request\-oriented entry point: closing the body is left to the server, so callers get a bounded, single\-shot decode. For an explicit, caller\-chosen limit use DecodeJSONMax.

The applied body limit depends on context. When r was handled by stdwrapper, the wrapper has already capped the body to its own Config.MaxBodyBytes \(see stdwrapper.BodyLimitFromContext\), so DecodeJSON defers to that cap and adds none of its own — the decode reflects the handling wrapper's limit rather than a fixed default. When no wrapper is present \(standalone use\), DecodeJSON applies stdwrapper.DefaultMaxBodyBytes as its own guard.

Decoding is strict: unknown fields are rejected and the body must contain exactly one JSON value with no trailing data. On any failure DecodeJSON returns the zero value of T and a \*stderr.StdErr with HTTP status 400 and no application error code, so a handler can return it directly for a 400 or re\-wrap it to attach a code of its own.

A nil request, or a request with no body, is treated as an empty payload and reported as a bad\-request error rather than panicking.

### Usage

```
func create(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (any, error) {
    body, err := httpkit.DecodeJSON[CreateUser](r)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err // 400 via stdwrapper
    }
    return store.Create(r.Context(), body)
}
```

<a name="DecodeJSONMax"></a>
## func [DecodeJSONMax](<https://github.com/xwinata/gorontalo/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/decodejson.go#L65>)

```go
func DecodeJSONMax[T any](r *http.Request, maxBytes int64) (T, error)
```

DecodeJSONMax is DecodeJSON with an explicit body size limit in bytes. A maxBytes of zero or less disables the limit, decoding the body unbounded; only do that for trusted input. All other behavior — strict decoding and the 400 \*stderr.StdErr on failure — matches DecodeJSON.

<a name="DecodeJSONReader"></a>
## func [DecodeJSONReader](<https://github.com/xwinata/gorontalo/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/decodejson.go#L79>)

```go
func DecodeJSONReader[T any](body io.Reader) (T, error)
```

DecodeJSONReader decodes a single JSON value from body into a value of type T. It is the reader\-oriented counterpart to DecodeJSON for callers that have already bounded or otherwise prepared the stream \(for example with their own io.LimitReader\), or that are decoding something other than an \*http.Request.

It applies the same strict rules as DecodeJSON — unknown fields rejected, exactly one value, no trailing data — and returns the same \*stderr.StdErr \(HTTP 400, no application code\) on failure. A nil body is reported as a bad\-request error rather than panicking.
